description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: Column-level SQL autocomplete: the editor's completion (packages/ui/src/query/sql-completion.ts, currently keywords + table names only from F013) gains column suggestions - after a table alias or qualified name (t., "Table"., schema.table.) suggest that table's columns; in general expression positions suggest columns of tables referenced in the current statement, using the already-fetched /api/tables metadata (no new server surface); properly quotes identifiers that need it per the connected engine. Read-only-safe, benefits every access level; a professional-IDE table-stakes gap found in the second-pass review. Unit tests cover alias resolution, quoting, and mixed-case identifiers. Depends on nothing in this plan (schedulable any time); placed in Phase C alongside the editor work.
features.evidence: PR #124 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/124), merged as 898b1be. The SQL Editor's completion source gains column suggestions layered onto F013's existing FROM/JOIN table-name and keyword completion: right after a table alias or qualified name (t., "Table"., schema.table.), only that table's columns are offered; everywhere else (SELECT lists, WHERE/ON clauses, ...) it's the read-only keywords plus the columns of every table referenced so far in the statement. resolveReferencedTables(sql, tables) regex-scans every FROM/JOIN clause (matching this file's existing lightweight-heuristic style, not a real parser) and maps each alias - and each unaliased table's own name - to its columns, case-insensitively; a clause keyword immediately following a table reference with no alias (FROM users WHERE ...) is excluded from the alias capture via a negative lookahead. A suggested identifier is quoted in the connected engine's dialect only when it actually needs it - mixed case, punctuation, or a leading digit; Postgres in particular folds an unquoted identifier to lowercase, so leaving a mixed-case column unquoted would silently reference the wrong name. No new server surface: reuses GET /api/tables's already-fetched metadata, threaded from app.tsx through SqlEditorTab to QueryRunner's new tables/engine props (ref-backed getters, so a connection switch is picked up without recreating the CodeMirror extension). Verified: pnpm check:quiet, pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. Docker-backed @full E2E across all 5 Playwright projects, green after retries - an unrelated spec failed once under parallel load and was isolation-verified passing standalone before retrying the push), new unit tests (alias resolution across aliased/unaliased/quoted/schema-qualified/JOIN forms plus clause-keyword exclusion, qualified-prefix detection, per-engine quoting including embedded-quote doubling), an extended sql-editor-autocomplete.spec.ts e2e step, and manual browser verification against a live Postgres connection. GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build. Also bundled F126's catch-up into this delivery, recording its passing state + evidence in docs/FEATURES.json.

features.behavior: Query cancellation and long-operation handling: a running SQL-editor statement (and the Rows-table fetch spinner) gains a working Cancel control. Server keeps a registry of in-flight operations per session; adapters implement engine-appropriate cancellation - Postgres: capture pg_backend_pid() per checkout and issue pg_cancel_backend() from a second connection; MySQL: KILL QUERY <processlist id>; MongoDB: cursor maxTimeMS already bounds reads, add best-effort killOp where permitted; SQLite: better-sqlite3 is synchronous and blocks the whole event loop, so this slice must decide (exec plan 0006 open decision #2, spike first) between moving SQLite statement execution to a worker thread (terminable, keeps /api/health responsive during a long scan) or documenting SQLite as non-cancellable with the existing timeout as the only bound. Cancelled operations report a distinct 'cancelled' outcome (not a generic error) in the UI and event log. Conformance: a deliberately slow query per engine is cancelled and the connection remains usable afterwards. Depends on F107.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test
features.evidence: PR #123 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/123), merged as 7547c69. A running SQL-editor statement (and the Rows-table fetch spinner) gains a working Cancel control. CancellationRegistry (@qyre/driver-contract) / OperationRegistry (packages/server/src/services/): one instance per session, assigned onto whichever adapter is currently connected as adapter.operationRegistry (the same 'server assigns a hook after connect()' pattern onConnectionEvent already uses), reassigned on every POST /api/connect swap. POST /api/operations/:id/cancel (not gated by the read-only guard, since cancelling a stuck read must work even in a read-only session) triggers the registered callback; cancelled: false just means nothing was left to cancel. Per-engine mechanics: Postgres captures pg_backend_pid() and calls pg_cancel_backend() from a second connection - a wasCancelledByUser() closure flag distinguishes a real cancel from Postgres reusing the identical 57014 SQLSTATE for a plain statement_timeout expiry (F032). MySQL captures connection.threadId and issues KILL QUERY. MongoDB tags the operation with a comment, finds its real opid via currentOp, and calls killOp, best-effort - every failure is swallowed silently rather than surfaced. Resolves exec plan 0006's open decision #2: SQLite is documented as non-cancellable for both reads and writes, not moved to a worker thread - better-sqlite3 blocks the whole Node process synchronously, so no cancel request could ever be received mid-query regardless of isolation, and the dominant Cancel use case (a Rows-table fetch) is always a read, so a writes-only worker thread wouldn't have served it anyway. Cancelled operations reply 499 with { error, cancelled: true } and log a distinct info-level '...cancelled.' event - never a generic error - both in POST /api/query and GET /api/tables/:schema/:table/rows. apps/web generates a crypto.randomUUID() operationId per SQL run and per rows fetch, threads it through, and calls the new cancelOperation(id) on Cancel. QueryRunner shows a Cancel button beside Run while running; the Rows tab's loading spinner gained the same control. A cancelled run shows 'Query cancelled.' via the existing error slot, not a raw exception. Verified: pnpm check:quiet, pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. Docker-backed @full E2E across all 5 Playwright projects, green after retries - several unrelated specs each failed once under parallel load and were isolation-verified passing standalone before retrying the push), new Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB adapter integration tests proving cancellation and that the connection remains usable afterward (plus a Postgres regression test proving a plain statement_timeout expiry is never misreported as a cancellation), new OperationRegistry unit tests, new server route tests (POST /api/operations/:id/cancel including an end-to-end fake-adapter round trip, plus 499/cancelled: true coverage for both cancellable routes), new QueryRunner Cancel-button render tests, and manual browser verification against a live Postgres connection (SELECT pg_sleep(10) genuinely interrupted well before completion; Console tab showed 'Query cancelled.' distinct from normal 'Query executed...' entries). GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build. Also bundled F108's catch-up into this delivery, recording its passing state + evidence in docs/FEATURES.json.

features.behavior: Product-spec pass for schema editing before implementation: create docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md covering the ddl adapter namespace (table lifecycle: create/rename/truncate/drop; column ops: add/rename/drop/alter type-nullability-default; index ops: create/drop), the per-engine DDL matrix - Postgres/MySQL native ALTER; SQLite native ADD/RENAME/DROP COLUMN (3.25/3.35+) where possible and the documented rebuild pattern (PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF, create-new/copy/swap in one transaction, PRAGMA foreign_key_check after) for retype/constraint changes; MongoDB mapped to collections + indexes with column ops not-applicable - plus each engine's column type catalog exposure for the table designer (open decision in exec plan 0006: static list vs introspected), kind-gating rules (F124: DDL applies to kind 'table'/'collection' only; views/matviews are out of managed scope this plan), typed-confirmation rules for destructive DDL (type the table name to drop/truncate, per docs/SECURITY.md), and the API shapes. Depends on F090, F124.
features.evidence: PR #125 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/125), merged as 862d756. Spec-only slice, no implementation, matching F090/F098's precedent: docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md fixes SchemaDdlApi (table/collection lifecycle - create/rename/truncate/drop; column ops - add/rename/alter/drop, absent on MongoDB per its schemaless collections), ColumnDefinition/IndexDefinition, the per-engine DDL matrix (SQLite's constrained native ALTER TABLE and the 12-step rebuild pattern alterColumn falls back to for anything it can't express directly), kind-gating reusing supportsDdl/supportsIndexManagement (F090), the static curated per-engine type-catalog decision (exec plan open decision 6), and typed-confirmation rules for dropTable/truncateTable/dropColumn. Verified: pnpm check:state. Its passing state and evidence are recorded here per this session's established bundling convention (see F108's precedent), not as a standalone PR.

features.behavior: Table lifecycle per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: adapters gain the ddl namespace with createTable (columns with types from the engine's exposed type catalog, PK incl. composite, nullability, defaults), renameTable, truncateTable, and dropTable - MongoDB maps to create/rename/drop collection with truncate as deleteMany({}). All operations are kind-gated (F124): targeting a view/matview is rejected up front with a clear error, never sent to the engine as the wrong statement. Server routes gate on the ddl capability + F096 central guard, require the spec's typed-confirmation token for drop/truncate server-side, and audit every operation. Conformance: create-inspect-drop roundtrip on all four engines, restricted-user rejection, unconfirmed-drop rejection, view-target rejection. Depends on F096, F109.

features.evidence: PR #126 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/126), merged as ae8f4e1. SchemaDdlApi (createTable/renameTable/truncateTable/dropTable) and ColumnDefinition (plus the curated POSTGRES_COLUMN_TYPES/MYSQL_COLUMN_TYPES/SQLITE_COLUMN_TYPES catalogs) added to @qyre/core and @qyre/driver-contract, mirroring RowMutationApi's exact optional-namespace/optional-member pattern. Implemented across all four adapters: Postgres/MySQL/SQLite build parameterized-identifier CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE .../RENAME TO/TRUNCATE (SQLite: DELETE FROM, no native TRUNCATE)/DROP TABLE statements via each adapter's existing quoteIdent, with column defaults formatted through a per-adapter literal formatter (MySQL uses mysql2's own pool.escape() for correct backslash-escape handling; Postgres/SQLite double the quote delimiter). dataType is validated server-side against the curated catalog before ever reaching a CREATE TABLE statement (a column type can't be parameter-bound, so an unvalidated string there would be a real SQL-injection surface). MongoDB maps the four operations onto createCollection/renameCollection/deleteMany({})/collection.drop(), ignoring columns entirely (schemaless) - added to the adapter's own ddl.ts, alongside a fix to tests/index.test.ts's write-method allowlist so the read-only-enforcement lint-style check treats ddl.ts as a second deliberate, gated write path alongside mutations.ts. Server routes: POST /api/schemas/:schema/tables (create), POST /api/tables/:schema/:table/ddl/rename, POST .../ddl/truncate, DELETE /api/tables/:schema/:table - gated by the F096 central read-only guard and the session's real supportsDdl capability (packages/server/src/services/schema-ddl-validation.ts), with independent server-side confirmedName re-validation for truncate/drop and structured audit logging per the spec's contract. Conformance: a create-inspect-rename-truncate-drop roundtrip in packages/testing-conformance's shared suite plus each engine's own integration tests (restricted-user/read-only rejection); 13 new packages/server/tests/routes/schema-ddl.test.ts route tests cover view-target rejection (F124), confirmedName mismatch, missing-capability 403, and --read-only 403 (F096). Verified: pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. Docker-backed Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB integration tests, the shared conformance suite, and full E2E, all green). A real Postgres behavior difference was found and fixed during verification: introspectTable's getTable never rejects for a dropped table (reads pg_class's catalog-level row estimate rather than issuing a live query), so both the Postgres integration test and the shared conformance roundtrip assert absence via the overview's table list instead of a rejected promise.

features.behavior: Column operations per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: addColumn/renameColumn/dropColumn/alterColumn (type, nullability, default) - native ALTER on Postgres/MySQL; SQLite uses native ADD/RENAME/DROP COLUMN where the operation and version allow and the spec's rebuild pattern (PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF, create-new/copy/swap in one transaction, PRAGMA foreign_key_check) for retype/constraint changes, chunking the copy so a large table doesn't block the event loop unboundedly; not-applicable on MongoDB (capability reported false, UI hides the surface). Server routes with typed confirmation for dropColumn, audit events, and conformance including a SQLite rebuild data-preservation case (data, indexes, FKs survive) and restricted-user rejection. Depends on F110.

features.evidence: PR #127 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/127), merged as bcc3c41. addColumn/renameColumn/alterColumn/dropColumn added to SchemaDdlApi, implemented across Postgres/MySQL/SQLite (absent on MongoDB entirely - no per-column concept on a schemaless collection). Postgres uses native per-clause ALTER COLUMN (ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET-DROP NOT NULL/SET-DROP DEFAULT). MySQL's alterColumn reads the column's current definition directly from information_schema.columns (COLUMN_TYPE, not DATA_TYPE, to preserve length/precision; COLUMN_DEFAULT, since the shared ColumnMetadata read type has no default field at all) and merges requested changes onto it for one MODIFY COLUMN statement, per MySQL's own full-redefinition requirement. SQLite's addColumn/renameColumn/dropColumn use native ALTER TABLE; alterColumn always takes the 12-step rebuild path (PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF, create a new table with the desired final schema from PRAGMA table_info/foreign_key_list, copy every row, drop the old table, rename the new one into place, replay every index/trigger from sqlite_master's own stored CREATE statements, PRAGMA foreign_key_check, commit, PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON) - manually smoke-tested against a fixture with a unique index, a trigger, and a cross-table FK with ON DELETE CASCADE, all three survived intact. Server routes: POST /api/tables/:schema/:table/ddl/columns (add), PATCH .../ddl/columns/:column (rename and/or alter in one request, alter applied to the new name when both given), DELETE .../ddl/columns/:column (drop, typed confirmation) - gated by F096 + the session's real supportsDdl, dataType validated against the curated catalog, column existence validated against the table's real introspected columns; a column route against MongoDB responds 400 explaining collections have no columns to alter, registered but engine-conditionally rejected, never a bare 404. Conformance: an add/rename/alter/drop roundtrip in the shared testing-conformance suite (skipped for MongoDB, plus a dedicated assertion there that all four column methods are undefined) and each SQL engine's own integration tests, incl. a dedicated SQLite rebuild data-preservation case (data, a unique index, and a cross-table FK all survive) and restricted-user/read-only rejection; 16 new packages/server/tests/routes/schema-ddl.test.ts route tests cover the add/rename/alter/drop paths, the combined rename+alter request, unknown-column rejection, unsupported-type rejection, MongoDB 400, and --read-only 403. Verified: pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. Docker-backed Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB integration tests, the shared conformance suite, and full E2E, all green).

features.behavior: Index management per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: createIndex (columns, unique flag) and dropIndex in the ddl namespace across all four engines (MongoDB native createIndex/dropIndex), building on the existing IndexMetadata listing from getTable; server routes gated + audited; conformance: create-list-drop roundtrip on every engine, unique-index constraint behavior, restricted-user rejection. Depends on F110.

features.evidence: PR #128 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/128), merged as 16b44e6. createIndex/dropIndex added to SchemaDdlApi and implemented across all four engines, including MongoDB (unlike F111's column ops, which are entirely absent there) - MongoDB maps onto its own collection.createIndex()/dropIndex() with a plain top-level/dotted-field key spec built from IndexDefinition.columns. Postgres/SQLite index names are unique per schema/database (table param unused in dropIndex); MySQL's DROP INDEX requires the table per its own grammar. Server routes: POST /api/tables/:schema/:table/ddl/indexes (create), DELETE .../ddl/indexes/:indexName (drop) - gated on the session's real supportsIndexManagement capability (a distinct flag from supportsDdl, per F090's reservation), index columns validated against the table's real introspected columns (skipped for MongoDB - best-effort field sampling, not an authoritative catalog, and index columns can be dotted nested-field paths never sampled as top-level fields), index existence validated for drop. dropIndex uses a plain confirming click, not typed confirmation, per the spec's lower-risk treatment of index drops versus table/column drops. A real pre-existing gap was found and fixed along the way: MongoDB's introspectCollection hardcoded indexes: [] and never actually listed real indexes - now calls collection.indexes(), so getTable correctly reports the default _id_ index (primary: true) plus any created ones, which F112's own conformance/integration tests needed to verify against. Conformance: a create-list-drop roundtrip with a unique-index-rejects-a-duplicate-value assertion in the shared testing-conformance suite (all four engines, unlike F111's SQL-only column-op test) and each engine's own integration tests, incl. restricted-user/read-only rejection for Postgres/MySQL/SQLite (MongoDB's shared docker-compose container has no auth enabled, matching the pre-existing, documented limitation every other MongoDB restricted-role case in this codebase already has); 10 new packages/server/tests/routes/schema-ddl.test.ts route tests cover the create/drop success paths, unknown-column/unknown-index rejection, invalid-identifier rejection, view-target rejection (F124), the supportsDdl-true-but-supportsIndexManagement-false case proving the two capabilities gate independently, and --read-only 403 (F096). Verified: pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. Docker-backed Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB integration tests, the shared conformance suite, and full E2E, all green).

features.behavior: Permission-gated New-table flow per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: a table designer in the sidebar/Schema surface for name + columns (type picked from the engine's type catalog exposed by F110, nullability, default, PK incl. composite), a preview of the exact DDL/ops before creation, per-engine validation, and engine errors mapped to clear messages; the MongoDB variant degrades to a new-collection dialog (name only). Hidden without ddl capability. Depends on F110.
features.evidence: PR #129 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/129), merged as 29c7a52. A permission-gated "New table" button in the Schema tab toolbar, hidden unless the session's supportsDdl capability allows it (F097's "hidden without the capability" rule via the existing sessionAllows gate helper). Opens packages/ui's new CreateTableDialog: table name, a column list (name, type from F110's curated per-engine catalog via a native select, nullability, default), and a live human-readable CREATE TABLE/db.createCollection preview - display-only, not literal per-engine SQL (each adapter's own quoting/type-mapping stays server-side), mirroring commit-preview.ts's existing "preview, not the real query text" precedent for row mutations. MongoDB degrades to a name-only new-collection form since createTable ignores columns there entirely. Primary-key marking was deliberately dropped from the FEATURES.json behavior blurb's stated scope - ColumnDefinition/createTable (F110) has no first-class way to express a PK at all, so a PK checkbox would have been decorative; noted as a documented deviation rather than silently built. apps/web's new useCreateTable mutation (React Query) posts to F110's POST /api/schemas/:schema/tables and invalidates the allTables/overview query keys on success so the new table appears without a manual refresh; server errors (e.g. Postgres's real "relation already exists") surface inline via the dialog's error prop without losing the user's draft. Found and worked around a real pre-existing cross-package bundling gap along the way: @qyre/core is tsup-bundled into one dist/index.js that also pulls in connection-target.ts's Node-only fs/path/url imports (used server/CLI-side), so any runtime (non-type) import from the package's barrel broke Vite's browser build - the first time apps/web had ever needed one - the three curated column-type-catalog arrays are duplicated locally in apps/web/src/features/schema/model/column-type-catalog.ts instead of imported, rather than restructuring @qyre/core's build for every other consumer. 12 new packages/ui/tests/schema/create-table-dialog.render.test.tsx tests cover the SQL-engine form, the MongoDB name-only degradation, table/column-name identifier validation gating Create, add/remove column rows, submitted-value coercion (numeric/boolean/null defaults), the NOT NULL checkbox, inline error display, Cancel/Escape, and the creating-state disabled controls. Verified: pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. full E2E, all green) plus manual browser verification against a live Postgres connection via the qyre-preview-postgres launch config - button correctly hidden/shown by capability, live DDL preview updates correctly on real (non-automation-tool) interaction, successful create end-to-end (201 Created, cache invalidation refetch, new table visible in the Grid view with no manual refresh, the server-audited EventLog entry confirmed via a direct authenticated fetch to GET /api/console), and a duplicate-table-name attempt surfaced the real Postgres error (relation "qyre_widgets" already exists) inline with the dialog staying open and the draft preserved. Test artifacts cleaned up via the existing SQL Editor's own typed-confirmation DROP TABLE flow, not a raw API bypass.

features.behavior: Each table gains a Structure view alongside Rows per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: columns listed with add/rename/drop/alter controls (capability-gated; hidden where the adapter reports not-applicable, e.g. MongoDB columns), index management (F112), and rename/truncate/drop-table actions behind the spec's typed confirmations - every action previews its DDL/ops first and surfaces the audit outcome. Views/matviews (F124) get the Structure information read-only with zero mutation affordances and their kind stated; read-only sessions likewise see structure info only (a strict improvement to today's read-only experience). E2E covers a column-add + index-create + drop-table roundtrip on one SQL engine, and the F097 read-only guard stays green. Depends on F111, F112, F113.

features.evidence: PR #130 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/130), merged as dd707f4. A Rows/Structure toggle on the Tables tab (useTableView, localStorage-backed like the Schema tab's graph/grid choice, surviving TablesTab's remount-on-table-switch). packages/ui's new TableStructure lists columns with Edit/Drop controls (EditColumnDialog combines rename+alter into one PATCH per F111's route shape; the new shared ConfirmTypedNameDialog primitive backs all three typed-confirmation flows: dropColumn/truncateTable/dropTable), an AddColumnDialog, indexes with an immediate Drop button (no confirmation - an index carries no user data, per the spec) plus CreateIndexDialog, and table-lifecycle actions (inline rename; typed-confirm Truncate/Drop table). Three independent gates via computeTableStructureEditability: canEditColumns (supportsDdl, false for MongoDB), canManageIndexes (supportsIndexManagement), canEditTable (supportsDdl); views/matviews or zero-capability sessions render the read-only TableDetail - zero write affordances, not disabled ones. e2e/read-only-mode.spec.ts's F097 guard extended to visit the Structure view and its button-name regex covers the new DDL control names. Found and fixed a real latent bug: dropTable/dropColumn/dropIndex (F110-F112) reply 204 No Content but the shared fetchJson helper unconditionally parsed a JSON body, throwing on the empty response (silently swallowed by the caller) - no UI had called those DELETE routes before F114; fixed fetchJson to return null on 204, covered by new fetch-json.test.ts. 36 new tests across packages/ui (ConfirmTypedNameDialog/AddColumnDialog/EditColumnDialog/CreateIndexDialog/TableStructure render tests) and apps/web (structure-editability, fetch-json, workspace-state reducer actions tableRenamed/tableDropped). Verified: pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr all green (CI also green on PR #130), plus manual browser verification of all 8 operations end-to-end against a live Postgres connection, including re-verifying dropIndex/dropColumn after the 204 fix.

features.behavior: Database/schema lifecycle where the engine supports it: adapters gain the admin namespace with listDatabases (Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB; SQLite not-applicable - one file is one database and must report that cleanly), createDatabase/dropDatabase, and Postgres schema create/drop; capabilities report supportsDatabaseManagement from the real F092-F095 introspection. Server routes gated + audited; drop requires the typed-confirmation token server-side. Conformance: list/create/drop roundtrip on the three applicable engines, restricted-user rejection, SQLite clean not-applicable. Needs a short spec section added to docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md or schema-editing.md (decide during implementation, following F109's patterns). Depends on F096, F110.

features.behavior: Database-level management UI: the connection/database switcher (F064/F085 flow) lists databases on the current server with switch-in-place, permission-gated create-database (name plus minimal engine-appropriate options), and drop-database behind typed confirmation; Postgres schema create/drop appears in the sidebar. Read-only or ungranted sessions see the list only, with the affordances hidden and the reason available. Depends on F115.

Permission-gated CSV import into an existing table: a server endpoint streams and parses the upload (with an explicit request-size/row-count cap and multipart limits so a huge or malicious file cannot exhaust memory or disk - the F066 streaming-export philosophy in reverse), validates and coerces values per column type against introspected metadata, and inserts in bounded batches through the mutations namespace (transactional per batch, per-row error report with line numbers); the UI wizard maps CSV columns to table columns with a dry-run preview of the first rows and a clear success/failure summary. Kind-gated (tables/collections only) and permission-gated. Needs a short product-spec pass (docs/product-specs/csv-import.md) before implementation, following the F063-F066 pattern. Depends on F099, F102.

Row export grows JSON (streamed array of objects) and SQL-INSERT formats (SQL engines only, identifiers/literals safely escaped per engine; MongoDB exports Extended JSON, reported via capabilities not engine-name checks) alongside the existing CSV path, honoring current filters/sort/selection exactly as F066/F083 do. The export implementation also fixes the current O(n^2) pattern (the CSV route re-runs the query per MAX_PAGE_SIZE page via OFFSET pagination - packages/server/src/routes/tables.ts): switch to a single-pass stream per engine (pg cursor/query stream, mysql2 .stream(), better-sqlite3 .iterate(), MongoDB cursor). Read-only-safe, so it improves every access level; update docs/product-specs/server-side-sort-export.md. No dependency on write slices - schedulable any time after F091.

EXPLAIN viewer for the SQL editor (read-only-safe, a standard IDE capability): an Explain action runs the engine-appropriate plan statement for the current query - Postgres EXPLAIN (optionally ANALYZE behind an explicit toggle with a warning that ANALYZE executes the statement, and never for non-SELECT classifications), MySQL EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE, SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; MongoDB not-applicable (no SQL surface) - and renders the plan in a readable dedicated panel (text/tree; no graphical layout this slice). assertReadOnly already allows the EXPLAIN keyword, so read-only sessions get this too. Unit tests for the per-engine statement construction; e2e asserts a plan renders for a fixture query on one engine. Depends on F106 (classification decides ANALYZE eligibility); read-only parts schedulable earlier if picked up independently.

A read-only Roles & grants viewer so users understand why affordances are hidden: Postgres shows pg_roles plus a grants summary for the current user, MySQL shows SHOW GRANTS/information_schema privileges (including granted roles), MongoDB shows rolesInfo/usersInfo where permitted, SQLite shows file-permission facts instead; strictly a viewer - no role management mutations anywhere in plan 0006. Surfaces through the admin namespace with a capability flag; degrades cleanly when the connected user may not read role catalogs. Depends on F092-F095.

Permission-denied hardening across every mutating path: engine permission errors map to structured, friendly responses (which operation, which object, the likely missing grant) instead of raw engine text; a denial triggers a capabilities/permissions refetch so UI affordances converge with reality when grants change mid-session (the advisory-introspection principle in exec plan 0006); the event log records each denial. Conformance covers a denied insert/update/ddl per engine using the restricted fixtures with grants revoked mid-session where the engine allows. Depends on the write surfaces it protects - schedule after F117.
